findings.title: FGAP listener breaks under V2 (UnsupportedOperationException)
findings.body: registerListener now guards only on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ but then calls management(...).clients()/roles()/groups().setPermissionsEnabled(). When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whose ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (and likely other V2 variants) throws UnsupportedOperationException. So with V2 enabled (alone with V1, or both V1+V2 enabled) any ClientRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent will throw from the event listener and break deletion. The guard must exclude V2 or handle V2 no-op.

findings.title: Resource lookup uses wrong owner, per-client and global checks miss
findings.body: hasPermission(ClientModel,String) does resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()) and hasPermission(String) does findByName(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, server.getId()). Resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource/init with owner resourceServer.getClientId() (or no owner for type resources) and looked up elsewhere with findByName(server, name) with no owner. Filtering by server.getId() as owner will not match, so per-instance resources are treated as missing and the global Clients type resource in hasPermission(String) is never found, making canManage()/canView()/canManageClientScopes() always false for V2 grants.

findings.title: Null dereference when all-clients resource is missing
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel,String) when the per-client resource is null the code does resource = SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) and then immediately calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource). getResourceTypeResource returns null if the Clients type resource does not exist. Passing null resource to findByResource causes NPE instead of denying permission.

findings.title: Global all-clients grant ignored once per-client resource exists
findings.body: hasPermission(ClientModel,String) evaluates only one resource: if an instance resource for the client exists it evaluates that resource alone; only if it is missing does it fall back to the Clients type resource. So a caller with a valid all-clients permission (e.g. MAP_ROLES/MANAGE/VIEW on type Clients) is denied for any client that happens to have its own resource object created for a different scope. Correct evaluation must OR the instance-resource decision with the type-resource decision.

findings.title: getResourceName does not handle Clients resource type
findings.body: getResourceName only resolves USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE to a username (or 'All users') and falls through to resource.getDisplayName() for everything else. After adding CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, client permission resources (whose name is the client UUID and which never get a displayName in getOrCreateResource/init) return null/meaningless names, and a deleted client does not raise a clear error like the user path does. It needs a CLIENTS branch resolving clientId similarly.
